desc:
You are given an integer array nums and a positive integer step. In one operation you pick any element and either add step to it or subtract step from it. You may perform any number of operations, on any elements, and elements are allowed to become negative.

The MEX of an array is the smallest non-negative integer that does not occur in it. Return the largest MEX you can obtain.

For example, nums = [1, -10, 7, 13, 6, 8] and step = 5 give 4: the elements can become 0, 1, 2, 3 (for instance -10 → 0, 1 → 1, 7 → 2, 13 → 3), but no element is congruent to 4 modulo 5, so 4 can never appear.
hints: Adding or subtracting step never changes x mod step. So an element can become the target value t exactly when x mod step == t mod step.
Count how many elements fall into each remainder class modulo step (use a non-negative remainder for negative numbers).

To reach MEX m you need distinct elements for the targets 0, 1, ..., m-1. Go through the targets in order, spend one element from class t mod step for each, and stop at the first target whose class is empty.
editorial: Because every move preserves the remainder modulo step, each element belongs forever to one class, and any non-negative target in its class is reachable. A target t is therefore coverable by any one element of class t mod step, and different targets need different elements.

Greedily process targets 0, 1, 2, ... : decrement the count of class t mod step and continue while it was positive. The first target that finds an empty class is the MEX. Every success consumes one element, so the loop runs at most n + 1 times, giving O(n + step) time (or O(n) with a dictionary of counts) and one counter per class.
